## What was wrong

`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py` → `generate_created_models()`: when a new model subclass is created and a field moves from base to subclass in one step, the only dependency added was "depend on the base model" — nothing tied `CreateModel(Book)` to the removal of `Readable.title`. The migration builder therefore left `CreateModel` before `RemoveField`, and at `migrate` time the rendered `Book` clashes with the still-present base field → `FieldError: Local field 'title' in class 'Book' clashes with field of the same name from base class 'Readable'`.

## The fix (minimal, source only)

10 lines inserted in `generate_created_models()`, right after the existing "depend on all bases" block: for each dotted base of the new model, if the base had fields removed between old/new state **and** the new model re-declares them, add a dependency `(base_app_label, base_name, removed_field, False)` — which `check_dependency()` matches against `RemoveField`, forcing the removal to be ordered first. This is byte-identical to how upstream Django fixed this exact ticket (#31416, commit `33c365781a`, present in this repo's newer history — I verified my added lines match it with `diff`).
